                             UNITED STATES DISTRICT COURT
                          FOR THE EASTERN DISTRICT OF VIRGINIA
                                  ALEXANDRIA DIVISION


  MARVELLE J. BALLENTINE,

                  Plaintiff,

                  V.                                            Case No. 1:26-cv-02331-RDA-IDD
                                                                The Honorable Judge
                                                                Rossie D. Alston Jr.


  KATIE HALL, individually;
  NATIONAL CENTER FOR MISSING & EXPLOITED CHILDREN;
  META PLATFORMS, INC.;
  and JOHN/JANE DOES 1-6,

                  Defendants.


           MEMORANDUM IN SUPPORT OF PLAINTIFF'S MOTION FOR LEAVE
                   TO FILE SUPPLEMENTAL COMPLAINT PURSUANT TO
                         FEDERAL RULE OF CIVIL PROCEDURE 15(d)
                                          INTRODUCTION

           Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 15(d) permits a party, on motion and reasonable notice, to

  serve a supplemental pleading setting out events that happened after the date of the pleading to be

  supplemented. Every event pleaded in Exhibit A occurred after the First Amended Complaint was

  filed.

           As to Count III, Exhibit A pleads that NCMEC's August 12, 2026 memorandum

  demonstrated actual knowledge of Plaintiff's pleaded injuries and disclosed survivor history and

  acknowledged that the person-level referent of the April 22, 2026 letters remains unresolved; that

  on August 13, 2026, counsel for NCMEC and Hall acknowledged that Plaintiff was upset and

Case 1:26-cv-02331-RDA-IDD            Document 27       Filed 08/21/26      Page 2 of 6 PageID# 321




  stated that Plaintiff "got exactly what you asked for"; and that the unresolved uncertainty

  continued.

           As to Count IV, Exhibit A pleads that on August 13, 2026, Meta Platforms, Inc. and the

  other Northern District of California defendants filed a consolidated motion to dismiss, ECF No.

  152, that expressly cited this action; that the filing described this matter as litigation against

  NCMEC and its corporate counsel; that Meta was already a named and served defendant here; that

  Count IV asserts a claim under 42 U.S.C. § 1985(2) against Meta concerning interference with

  Plaintiff's participation in that Northern District of California proceeding; and that the filing did

  not identify those facts. The event is pleaded as evidence of Meta's knowledge, state of mind, and

  awareness of the relationship between the two proceedings.

           The Motion is narrow. It involves the same parties, the same causes of action, and the same

  requested relief. It supplements two existing counts and leaves the First Amended Complaint

  otherwise unchanged. Leave should be granted.

                                           BACKGROUND

           A.   The First Amended Complaint

           The First Amended Complaint (ECF No. 5) is the operative pleading. Count III asserts

  intentional infliction of emotional distress against Defendants Hall and NCMEC. Count IV asserts

  a claim under the first clause of 42 U.S.C. § 1985(2) concerning alleged interference with

  Plaintiff's participation as a party and prospective witness in federal proceedings, including the

  proceeding now pending as Ballentine v. Meta Platforms, Inc., No. 3:26-cv-05939-RFL (N.D.

  Cal.).

           B.   The August 12-13, 2026 NCMEC and Hall Events

Case 1:26-cv-02331-RDA-IDD            Document 27        Filed 08/21/26      Page 3 of 6 PageID# 322




         On August 12, 2026, NCMEC filed its memorandum in support of its motion to dismiss.

  ECF No. 11. The memorandum expressly addressed the First Amended Complaint's allegations

  that Plaintiff is a survivor of childhood sexual abuse and that Plaintiff vomited, experienced

  recollections of childhood sexual abuse, and feared arrest and prosecution after receiving the April

  22, 2026 letters. The memorandum stated that Plaintiff "does not have access to those reports" and

  described the asserted CyberTipline linkage as one that could concern Plaintiff, "a person with the

  same name," or an email address.

         On August 13, 2026, Plaintiff asked counsel for NCMEC and Hall whether either report, as

  received, contained or identified his legal name, the name he uses, or his email identifier. Counsel

  did not provide an answer resolving the question, and wrote: "I read your email as being upset with

  the language used in the memorandum-I did not intend to offend you with the phrasing, but my

  point was you got exactly what you asked for, using the language you provided." The person-level

  uncertainty remains unresolved.

         C.   Meta's August 13, 2026 Northern District of California Filing

         On August 13, 2026, Meta Platforms, Inc., Accenture LLP, Genpact Limited, and TaskUs,

  Inc. jointly filed a consolidated motion to dismiss in No. 3:26-cv-05939-RFL. ECF No. 152. The

  filing expressly cited the present action and described it as "a complaint against the National Center

  for Missing & Exploited Children ('NCMEC') and its corporate counsel in the Eastern District of

  Virginia based on allegedly defamatory language in a letter sent by NCMEC to Plaintiff in

  response to a subpoena." ECF No. 152 at 4 n.3. When the filing was made, Meta was a named

  defendant in this action, served on July 31, 2026, and Count IV asserted a claim under 42 U.S.C. §

  1985(2) against Meta concerning Plaintiff's participation in the Northern District of California

Case 1:26-cv-02331-RDA-IDD           Document 27       Filed 08/21/26      Page 4 of 6 PageID# 323




  litigation. The filing did not identify Meta's status as a defendant here and did not identify that

  Count IV allegation.

                                       LEGAL STANDARD

         Rule 15(d) provides that, on motion and reasonable notice, the Court may, on just terms,

  permit a party to serve a supplemental pleading setting out any transaction, occurrence, or event

  that happened after the date of the pleading to be supplemented. Fed. R. Civ. P. 15(d).

         A supplemental pleading concerns matters occurring after the filing of the pleading being

  supplemented. The standards governing amendment under Rule 15(a) and supplementation under

  Rule 15(d) are nearly identical: leave should be freely granted, and denial requires a good reason,

  such as prejudice to the opposing party. Franks v. Ross, 313 F.3d 184, 198 n.15 (4th Cir. 2002).

                                            ARGUMENT

         I.      The Proposed Supplement Properly Pleads Subsequent Events Directly

                 Related to Existing Claims.

         A.      The August 12-13 Events Directly Supplement Count III.

         The August 12 and 13, 2026 events occurred after the First Amended Complaint was filed.

  They concern the Defendants already named in Count III. They concern those Defendants' post-

  filing knowledge of the injuries already pleaded, their acknowledged awareness that Plaintiff

  remained distressed, their continued possession of the information capable of resolving the

  uncertainty already alleged, and the continuing injury already pleaded. The supplement uses the

  post-filing events to bear on existing allegations concerning knowledge, intent or recklessness,

  outrageousness, and continuing injury. Exhibit A does not allege that the August 12 memorandum

  or the August 13 communication independently satisfies the elements of intentional infliction of

  emotional distress.

Case 1:26-cv-02331-RDA-IDD               Document 27    Filed 08/21/26     Page 5 of 6 PageID# 324




         B.     Meta's August 13 Filing Directly Supplements Count IV.

          Count IV already concerns alleged interference with Plaintiff's participation in federal

  proceedings, including the Northern District of California litigation. Meta's August 13, 2026 event

  occurred inside that same litigation. Meta affirmatively invoked the present action there. Meta was

  already a defendant here, and already faced Count IV, when it made the filing. The event therefore

  supplies a subsequent fact concerning Meta's actual knowledge and its awareness of the

  relationship between the two proceedings. The proposed Supplemental Complaint does not seek

  liability based on Meta's filing of ECF No. 152 or on any statement contained in that filing. The

  filing is alleged as evidence bearing on knowledge, notice, state of mind, and the existing

  circumstantial allegations supporting Count IV.

          II.     The Proposed Supplement Causes No Prejudice and Does Not Expand the

         Action.

          Six facts define the scope of the request. The supplement adds no new party. It adds no new

  cause of action. It adds no new relief. It supplements only Counts III and IV. The subsequent events

  it pleads were created by or on behalf of the existing Defendants -NCMEC's own memorandum,

  its counsel's own communication, and Meta's own filing- so their existence presents no surprise

  to any Defendant. And Plaintiff sought supplementation promptly after the events occurred. The

  First Amended Complaint remains otherwise unchanged. The proposed supplementation permits

  the existing controversy to be adjudicated on a factual record that includes subsequent events

  directly related to existing claims.

Case 1:26-cv-02331-RDA-IDD          Document 27        Filed 08/21/26     Page 6 of 6 PageID# 325




         III.    The Pending Rule 12 Posture Does Not Make Supplementation Futile.

         Rule 15(d) expressly permits subsequent events to be added to an existing pleading. The

  presence of pending Rule 12 motions does not change the temporal character or the relevance of

  those subsequent events.

         Exhibit A does not create independent causes of action from the post-filing litigation

  statements. For Count III, the subsequent events bear on existing issues of knowledge, state of

  mind, intent or recklessness, and continuing injury. For Count IV, Meta's filing bears on existing

  issues of knowledge, awareness, state of mind, and circumstantial evidence.

         The question this Motion presents is whether the subsequent events may be pleaded, not

  whether Counts III and IV ultimately succeed. The Court can grant leave without resolving the

  merits of either count.

                                          CONCLUSION

         The Court should grant Plaintiff leave under Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 15(d) to file

  the Proposed Supplemental Complaint attached as Exhibit A.
